# WebMCP: forms are agent tools

WebMCP is on by default (`"webmcp": true` in `pragma.json`; omitted means `true`). Every `<form>` is a declarative WebMCP tool. The browser registers the tool while the form is mounted and removes it when the form unmounts.

```html
<form toolname="search_products" tooldescription="Search the catalog by name or category" toolautosubmit @submit="search">
  <label for="query">Search</label>
  <input id="query" name="query" type="search" required toolparamdescription="Words to search for in product names and categories">
  <button class="btn btn-primary">Search</button>
</form>
```

| Attribute | Target | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `toolname` | `<form>` | Required with `tooldescription`. Lowercase `snake_case` `verb_object` (`search_products`, `add_task`, `create_order`), unique per page. |
| `tooldescription` | `<form>` | Required with `toolname`. One sentence of 4+ words describing action and purpose. |
| `toolparamdescription` | input, select, textarea | Describes the expected input. Without it, agents fall back to `<label>` text, then `aria-description`. `aria-label` is not read. |
| `toolautosubmit` | `<form>` | Submits without user click. Use only on safe, reversible forms (search, filter, add). Never on delete, pay, buy, cancel, send, or transfer. |
| `notool` | `<form>` | Excludes the form (login, password, payment). Removed at build time. |

- Add `name` to every field (`type=submit|reset|button|image` exempt).
- Use native constraints (`required`, `type`, `min`/`max`, `<select>` options) to describe parameters.
- Use static strings only; do not use `:` bindings or `{}` in tool attributes.
- Exception: a component passes a tool attribute on from its caller with `:toolparamdescription="$toolparamdescription"` (prop `export let toolparamdescription = ''`). The caller must write fixed text (`<c-select toolparamdescription="…">`); the build writes that text into the attribute.
- Without `toolautosubmit`, the browser fills the form and focuses the submit button for the user.
- With `"webmcp": false`, any tool attribute triggers `webmcp/disabled`.

## Result to the agent

`@submit="fn"` (no parentheses) passes the `SubmitEvent`. `event.agentInvoked` is `true` when an agent submits. Call `event.respondWith(promise)` before any `await`. Read fields from `new FormData(event.target)`, not `:model` state.

```html
<script>
  import { call } from 'pragma'

  let products = []

  async function search(event) {
    const query = new FormData(event.target).get('query')
    const reply = call('search', { query })
    if (event.agentInvoked) event.respondWith(reply)
    products = (await reply).products
  }
</script>
```

Return plain JSON (`{ products: [...] }`, `{ error: 'Use at least 3 characters.' }`). Respond with validation errors too so the agent can retry.

## CSS

`:tool-form-active` matches a form while an agent fills it. `:tool-submit-active` matches its submit button. `.pragma/base.css` styles both; override them in `lib/theme.css` or page `<style>`:

```css
form:tool-form-active { outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary-600); }
```

## Check rules (`webmcp/*`)

Errors (broken tool):

| Rule | Fix |
|---|---|
| `webmcp/pair` | Provide both `toolname` and `tooldescription`, or neither. |
| `webmcp/name` | Use 1–128 chars from `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -` in `toolname`. |
| `webmcp/duplicate` | Use a unique `toolname` per page (`<if>`/`<else>` branches count separately). |
| `webmcp/param-name` | Add `name` to every field in a tool form. |
| `webmcp/dynamic` | Use static text only in tool attributes (no `:` or `{}`). A component prop passed on with `:attr="$prop"` must get fixed text from the caller. |
| `webmcp/notool` | Use `notool` only on `<form>`, never with `toolname`. |
| `webmcp/attribute` | Put `tooldescription`/`toolautosubmit` only on `<form>`, and `toolparamdescription` only on input, select, or textarea. |
| `webmcp/disabled` | Remove tool attributes when `"webmcp": false`, or set `"webmcp": true`. |

Warnings (errors with `--strict`):

| Rule | Fix |
|---|---|
| `webmcp/form-tool` | Add `toolname` + `tooldescription`, or `notool`. |
| `webmcp/name-style` | Use lowercase `snake_case` `verb_object` with at least one `_` (`search_products`). |
| `webmcp/description` | Write 4+ words in `tooldescription`. |
| `webmcp/param-description` | Add `toolparamdescription`, `<label>`, or `aria-description` to the field. |
| `webmcp/autosubmit` | Remove `toolautosubmit` from destructive or financial tools (`delete_`, `remove_`, `destroy_`, `pay_`, `buy_`, `purchase_`, `cancel_`, `send_`, `transfer_`). |

## Disable WebMCP

Set `"webmcp": false` in `pragma.json` to disable `webmcp/*` checks (existing tool attributes then trigger `webmcp/disabled`). Prefer `notool` on individual forms.

## Markdown for agents

Non-browser agents request `text/markdown`. Add a `.md` file in `public/` matching the route: `public/index.md` for `/`, `public/pricing.md` or `public/pricing/index.md` for `/pricing`. When `Accept` prefers `text/markdown` (quality >= `text/html`), the server returns that `.md` file; otherwise it returns HTML.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/packages.md

# npm packages

Add a package only when the platform cannot do the task. Check `Intl`, `fetch`, `crypto.randomUUID`, `URLSearchParams`, and `structuredClone` first.

## Install

```sh
npm i date-fns --ignore-scripts
```

- List every imported package in `package.json` `dependencies`. Importing an unlisted package is an error.
- Use any package manager (npm, bun, pnpm); pragma reads `package.json` and `node_modules/`.
- Exclude `node_modules/` from git.

## Import

```js
import { format } from 'date-fns'

let today = format(new Date(), 'PPP')
```

- Use a quoted module specifier; do not use template literals.
- Import named exports from the index or a subpath. The build tree-shakes each ES module package.
- Each package outputs `/assets/npm/<package>-<hash>.js` (`@date-fns/tz` -> `date-fns__tz`) with `modulepreload`. Shared chunks go to `/assets/npm/_*.js`. Package size counts in the page JS size that `pragma build` prints.
- Avoid `import * as x from 'pkg'` and `import('pkg')` when possible; they bundle the whole package.
- To load a package only on use, import it in a `utils/` module and `import()` that module (`performance.md`, "Lazy-load heavy code").
- `process.env.NODE_ENV` evaluates to `"production"` in build and `"development"` in dev.

## Supported packages

Client code supports plain JS packages (`.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, plus imported `.json`) using ES modules or CommonJS. CommonJS packages cannot be tree-shaken and ship whole; prefer ES modules.

| Unsupported on client | Error |
|---|---|
| TypeScript, JSX, `.vue`, `.svelte`, imported CSS or assets | `app/package` |
| `node:*` or Node built-ins (`fs`, `path`) | `app/package` |
| Importing an export the package does not provide | `js/import` |
| UI frameworks (React, Preact, Vue, Svelte, Solid, lit, jQuery, Alpine) | `js/import` |

In `.server.js`, all `package.json` dependencies and Node built-ins (`fs`, `node:*`) work without extra listing. A built-in name listed in `package.json` (such as `buffer`) bundles as a package.

## WebAssembly (server only)

Import a `.wasm` file, from the project (`./_solver.wasm`) or from a package export (`highs/runtime`), in server code. The import gives a compiled `WebAssembly.Module` on Workers and on Node (`pragma dev`, `pragma serve`, `node.mjs`). The build copies the file to `dist/server/` and adds a `CompiledWasm` rule to `dist/server/wrangler.jsonc`. A root `wrangler.jsonc` needs no rule (wrangler treats `*.wasm` the same way by default).

```js
import loadHighs from 'highs'
import highsWasm from 'highs/runtime'

let loading

export function solver() {
  loading ??= loadHighs({
    instantiateWasm(imports, done) {
      WebAssembly.instantiate(highsWasm, imports).then(done)
      return {}
    },
  })
  return loading
}
```

- Workers cannot compile WebAssembly from bytes. Pass the imported module to the package (Emscripten packages: `instantiateWasm`).
- Importing `.wasm` in client code is a `js/import` error.

## Workers modules

`cloudflare:workers`, `cloudflare:sockets` and other `cloudflare:*` modules work in `.server.js` on Workers only. On Node (`pragma dev`, `pragma serve`, `node.mjs`) the server still starts: `env` from `cloudflare:workers` is the `env` that `load` and actions receive (with `pragma dev --cf`, the wrangler bindings), and every other import (`DurableObject`, `connect`, …) throws when it is used. In client code they are an `app/package` error. Prefer the `env` that `load` and actions receive.

## Recommended

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Format dates, numbers, currency, plurals, relative time | Native `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.PluralRules`, `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` |
| Date math (add, diff, start of month) | `date-fns`; time zones: `@date-fns/tz` |
| Form or payload validation | `valibot` |
| Fuzzy list search | `fuse.js` |
| Charts | `chart.js` (render into `<canvas>` in `.html`) |
| Debounce, throttle, group, sort | `es-toolkit` |
| Unique ID | Native `crypto.randomUUID()` |
| HTTP requests | Native `fetch` |

## Do not use

| Package | Reason | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| `moment` | Large, no tree-shaking | `date-fns`, `Intl` |
| `lodash` | CommonJS; ships whole (~25 kB gzip) | `es-toolkit` |
| `axios` | Large; redundant | `fetch` |
| `uuid`, `nanoid` | Redundant | `crypto.randomUUID()` |
| HTML-building libraries (`marked`, template engines, UI kits) | HTML in JS is forbidden | Markup in `.html` |

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/performance.md

# Performance

Pragma optimizes builds by default: prebuilt HTML, `load` fetch started in `<head>`, per-route CSS with only the theme rules the page can match (inlined in production when <= 14 kB gzip, so small pages have no render-blocking stylesheet), per-page font preload, per-route JS chunks, link prefetch and Speculation Rules, 103 Early Hints, precompressed `.br`/`.gz` assets, hashed immutable assets (JS, CSS, and the `public/` files that CSS names with `url()`, such as fonts), and unused CSS stripped. `pragma build` prints the JS gzip size of each page; it does not enforce limits.

## JS chunks

`pragma build` bundles the client JS (`pragma dev` keeps one file per module):

- The core runtime is one file (`/assets/core/boot-<hash>.js`).
- Each route gets one chunk with its page, components, stores and the code only it uses (`/assets/routes/<route>-<hash>.js`). Asset names are URL-safe: `[id]` becomes `_id_` (`/assets/css/app/_id_-<hash>.css`), so no asset URL gets a redirect.
- Code used by 2+ routes goes to `/assets/chunks/shared<nnn>-<hash>.js` (`shared000`, `shared001`, …), one chunk per set of routes. A set under 4 kB joins a chunk that a wider set of routes uses.
- `await import()` stays a separate chunk. npm packages stay in `/assets/npm/` (`packages.md`).
- The bodies of `<if>`, `<else-if>`, `<else>`, `<for>` and `<empty>` go to the page's template module (`/assets/tpl/<route>-<hash>.js`), and the page `modulepreload`s it. The prebuilt HTML keeps only a short comment where each block renders (`<!--p:if t3 state.open-->`), so a page with many blocks or long lists stays small. The browser parses a body only when a block first renders it.
- The page `modulepreload`s every chunk it runs. The router prefetches the HTML and chunks of a link on hover, focus, and when the link enters the viewport, also for links rendered after the page loads (`/app/:id` links included). Viewport prefetch starts after the `load` event, when the browser is idle, and is off when the user turns on Save-Data. The router requests the clean page URL (`/app`, not `/app/index.html`).

## Lazy-load heavy code

Code that runs only after a click (export to XLSX or PDF, a parser, a chart in a closed modal) does not need to be in the route chunk. Put it in a `utils/` module and load that module with `await import()` inside the action.

`utils/export-xlsx.js`:

```js
import { utils, writeFile } from 'xlsx'

export function exportXlsx(rows, name) {
  const book = utils.book_new()
  utils.book_append_sheet(book, utils.json_to_sheet(rows), 'Data')
  writeFile(book, name)
}
```

`routes/report.html`:

```html
<script>
  let rows = []

  async function download() {
    const { exportXlsx } = await import('../utils/export-xlsx.js')
    exportXlsx(rows, 'report.xlsx')
  }
</script>

<button type="button" @click="download">Export XLSX</button>
```

- `pragma build` puts the module in `/assets/chunks/<name>-<hash>.js` and the packages it imports in `/assets/npm/`. The page does not `modulepreload` them; the browser fetches them on the first click. `pragma dev` does the same per file.
- Import named exports in the `utils/` module, not `import('pkg')` in the page: the build tree-shakes the package only through named imports.
- Use `import()` only. A static `import` of the same module anywhere in the route (page, component, store) puts it back in the route chunk.
- It works the same in a component `<script>` (for example the action of a modal). The markup of the component stays in the route; only the imported code is lazy.
- The page JS size that `pragma build` prints does not count lazy chunks.
- Show a pending state if the first load can be slow (`let exporting = true` before the `await`).

## Rules

- Navigate with `<a href>`. A `<button>` that calls `navigate()` gets no prefetch.
- Match skeleton shapes to the final content.
- Set `width` and `height` on every `<img>`. Add `loading="lazy"` below the fold. Store AVIF or WebP images in `public/`.
- Set `font-display: swap` on custom fonts and declare them with `@font-face` in `lib/theme.css`, with the file in `public/` and a root path (`url('/fonts/x.woff2')`). The build serves the font from a hashed, immutable `/assets/` URL and preloads the fonts each page uses (`css.md`). Do not write `<link rel="preload" as="font">` in `_layout.html`.
- Give `<for>` a stable `key`.
- Drive per-frame animations (scroll, drag, progress) with `frame` from `'pragma'`: read layout first, then assign state (`state.md`, "Per-frame updates").
- Use per-frame `:--name` values only in `transform` and `opacity`, never in `top`/`left`/`width`/`height`/`margin`/`padding`/`inset` (`css.md`, "Values that change every frame").
- Omit `.js` on pages without interaction.
- Keep heavy single-page code on that page. Load interaction-only code with `await import()` inside the action ("Lazy-load heavy code").
- Return only displayed fields from `load`. Run independent requests with `Promise.all`.
- Keep page JS small. Read the size table of `pragma build` after you add a package or a large module.
- Do not import large modules in `lib/state/`. Do not fetch data in `mount`. Do not enable `ssr` by default.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/logs.md

# Logs

Pragma configures OpenTelemetry on client and server automatically.

- In page, component, and store scripts, import `log` from `'pragma'`.
- In `load` and server actions, use the `log` argument.
- In `utils/`, import `log` from `'../.pragma/log.js'`.

```js
import { call, params, log } from 'pragma'

let error = ''

async function save() {
  try {
    await call('save', { id: params.id })
    log.info('order saved', { 'order.id': params.id })
  } catch (failure) {
    log.error('order save failed', { 'order.id': params.id, 'exception.message': failure.message })
    error = 'Could not save.'
  }
}
```

| Level | Use when |
|---|---|
| `debug` | Diagnostics (shown in `pragma dev`; off in production unless `PRAGMA_LOG_LEVEL=debug`). |
| `info` | Business event. |
| `warn` | Recoverable problem. |
| `error` | Failure. |

## Rules

- Keep messages short and fixed. Put dynamic values in attributes (`order.id`, `exception.message`, `http.request.method`).
- Do not duplicate automatic logs: unhandled errors, navigation, fetch failures, request spans, and `traceparent`.
- In `pragma dev`, client `log.*` also prints to the browser console.
- Client logs send to `POST /_otel` in batches: 2 s after the first record, at 50 records, and with `sendBeacon` when the tab hides. On static hosts returning 404 or 405, the client stops sending.
- `log.flush()` sends the queued client records now. Call it only when the page must not wait for the next batch (before `location.assign` to another site). The server `log` has no `flush`: its records go out at the end of each request.
- Forbidden: `console.*`, logging inside loops or on every keystroke, and logging passwords, tokens, cookies, emails, or personal data.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/cli.md

# `pragma` CLI

| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| `pragma -V` | Prints the installed CLI version. |
| `pragma new <dir>` | Creates an app with the fixed structure. Warns and keeps existing files if `<dir>` is not empty. |
| `pragma dev [--port 5180] [--host 127.0.0.1] [--cf]` | Runs the dev server with WebSocket live reload. Shows an overlay on build errors while valid pages keep working. Starts Node >= 22 when `.server.js` exists. Prints `app/core-outdated` first if `.pragma/` is older than the CLI. `--cf`: Cloudflare bindings in dev (see below). |
| `pragma check [--strict]` | Checks JS, HTML, CSS, accessibility, and WebMCP tools. `--strict` turns warnings into errors. |
| `pragma build [--allow-outdated-core]` | Builds `dist/` and prints the JS gzip size of each page (information only, no limits). Stops with `app/core-outdated` if `.pragma/` is older than the CLI (`--allow-outdated-core` overrides this). |
| `pragma serve [--port 3000] [--host 127.0.0.1]` | Serves `dist/` as in production. |
| `pragma upgrade` | Syncs `.pragma/` (runtime, docs, `base.css`, `version`) with the installed CLI version. Prints updated, added, or removed files. Never edits files outside `.pragma/`. |
| `pragma self-update [version]` | Downloads the latest or specified `pragma` binary from GitHub Releases, verifies it with `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and replaces the executable. If the checksum is missing or wrong, it stops and does not change the binary. |

Run `pragma check --strict` before you finish. Fix all errors and warnings.
Output format: `file:line:column error|warning [rule] message`.
Fix the root cause; do not work around a rule.

## Versioning and updates

- `.pragma/version` stores the version of `.pragma/` in the app.
- Compare `pragma -V` with `.pragma/version`.
- If they differ, or if `pragma check` reports `app/core-outdated`, run `pragma upgrade`.
- Run `pragma self-update [version]` to update the CLI binary.

## Rules

| Rule | Fix |
|---|---|
| `js/syntax`, `html/syntax`, `css/syntax` | Write valid syntax. Close every non-void HTML tag. |
| `js/html-in-js` | Remove `innerHTML`, `createElement`, `document.write`. Put markup in `.html`. Strings with markup are allowed only in `.server.js` (e-mail bodies, LLM prompts). |
| `js/console` | Use `log.*` (`logs.md`). |
| `js/jsdoc-types` | Remove TypeScript and JSDoc types. |
| `js/import` | Import only project files, `.pragma/`, and `package.json` dependencies (`packages.md`). Pass a quoted specifier to `import()` (`import('./chart.js')`), never a variable or `${}`. |
| `js/comment`, `html/comment`, `css/comment` | Delete the comment. Use clear names. |
| `js/vague-name` | Use descriptive names. Avoid generic words (`tmp`, `data`, `info`, `handler`, `util`), names ending in a single digit (`item2`; multi-digit numbers and pairs like `12x36` are fine), and names under 3 chars except `$ i j k id ok el ctx url log db kv` (server context keys) and parameters of expression-body arrows. |
| `js/legacy-api` | Replace old API (`export const state`/`actions`, `export function mount`, `ctx.$`, `ctx.update`, `store()`). Use top-level `let`, functions, `function mount(el)`, and `export let` (`components.md`, `state.md`). |
| `js/prop-write` | Do not mutate props (including via `:model`). Copy into a `let` (`let current = start`). |
| `js/const-state` | Declare mutated state with `let`, not `const`. |
| `js/store-import` | Access stores through `shared` (`import { shared } from 'pragma'`, then `shared.cart`). |
| `js/component-script` | Follow script rules (`state.md`): no `var`, no destructuring `let`, only `export let` props (stores export only `persist`), no top-level `await`, only valid `pragma` imports, no `$`/`$pragma` declarations. |
| `js/top-level-data` | Read `data` inside functions (`const products = () => data.products`), not at top level. |
| `js/stale-derived` | Convert static derived values to functions (`const doubled = () => count * 2`), or update them in actions. |
| `js/derived-call` | Call derived functions in JS (`empty()`), not as bare values (`if (empty)`). |
| `js/dollar-in-script` | Write `x` in JS; `$x` is HTML only. |
| `html/legacy-syntax`, `html/unknown-directive` | Use pragma syntax (`syntax.md`). Replace foreign attributes (`v-if`, `x-show`, `v-bind:href`, `on:click`, `*ngIf`, `[disabled]`, `className`) with pragma forms (`<if path>`, `:show`, `:href`, `@click`). |
| `html/data-attribute` | Do not write `data-*` by hand. Use short forms (`{path}` instead of `data-text`), `:data-x="path"`, `.name="path"`, `aria-*`, or role/label/id. |
| `html/invalid-path`, `html/invalid-root` | Use `root.a.b` with a valid root (`syntax.md`). Close `{}` (`\{` for literal). Pass only paths, `'text'`, numbers, `true`/`false`/`null`, `event`, or `el` to events. Omit `$` in event names. Use bare paths in `:attr` and `<if>`. |
| `html/text-removed` | Replace `:text` with `{path}` inside the element (`<p>{$name}</p>`). |
| `html/block`, `html/block-single-root`, `html/for-without-key`, `html/misplaced-else`, `html/misplaced-empty`, `html/outside-template` | Follow block rules (`syntax.md`). |
| `html/unknown-name` | Declare the name at the top level of the owner script (`let x`, `export let x`, `function x()`). Layouts have no script. In `@click="shared.cart.x(…)"`, `x` must be a store function. |
| `html/unknown-prop` | Declare the prop in the component script (`export let name = default`). |
| `html/duplicate-module` | Use inline `<script>`/`<style>` or external `x.js`/`x.css`, not both. |
| `html/component`, `html/unknown-component` | Follow component rules (`components.md`). |
| `html/layout`, `html/title`, `html/head` | Follow layout and SEO rules (`routes.md`). |
| `html/css-var` | Write `:--name` in lowercase kebab-case. A static value cannot contain `;`, `{`, `}`, or `<` (`css.md`). |
| `html/class` | Toggle classes with `.name="path"`. Do not use `:class` or `{}` in `class` (`syntax.md`). |
| `html/interpolation` | Replace `{{ }}` and `${ }` with `{path}` (`syntax.md`). |
| `html/script`, `html/style-inline`, `html/on-inline` | Put at most one `<script>` (optional `type="module"`) and one `<style>` at the top level of a page or component `.html`. Replace `style="..."` with classes, or with `:--name="path"` and `var(--name)` in CSS (`css.md`). Put JSON-LD `<script type="application/ld+json">` only at the top level of a page (`routes.md`). |
| `html/json-ld` | Fix invalid JSON or unclosed `{` in JSON-LD strings. Use `{` for a literal brace. |
| `css/unknown-class`, `css/arbitrary-value` | Use classes from `classes.md` or custom classes per `css.md`. |
| `css/utility-name` | In `lib/theme.css`, do not write a rule whose selector is only a utility name (`.flex`, `.hidden:hover`). Rename the class (`css.md`). |
| `css/unmatched-selector` (warning) | A page or component selector matches no element its owner writes (slot content, child component markup). Wrap the outside part in `:global(…)` or move the style to the writer (`css.md`). |
| `app/structure`, `app/route-conflict` | Follow structure and route rules (`structure.md`, `routes.md`). |
| `app/endpoint`, `app/middleware` | An endpoint exports only `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`; the middleware exports `handle` (`data.md`). |
| `app/endpoint-json` (warning) | An endpoint answers JSON. Use `load` and actions for page data (`data.md`). |
| `app/package` | Follow package rules (`packages.md`). |
| `app/pragma-json` | Fix `pragma.json` (`structure.md`). |
| `app/output` | The build cannot write its output (`dist/`, `.pragma/dev/`). Check the folder permissions and the free disk space. |
| `app/core-outdated` (warning; error in `pragma build`) | `.pragma/` differs from the CLI version. Run `pragma upgrade`. Do not edit `.pragma/` by hand. |
| `internal` (`pragma dev`) | The compiler stopped with a bug. Report it with the file you changed last. |

## Accessibility (`a11y/*`, warnings; errors with `--strict`)

| Rule | Fix |
|---|---|
| `img-alt` | Add `alt` to every `<img>`. Use `alt=""` for decorative images. |
| `accessible-name` | Give `<button>` and `<a>` text, `{path}`, `aria-label`, or `title`. |
| `label` | Associate fields with `<label for>`, wrap in `<label>`, or add `aria-label`. |
| `dialog-name` | Add `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to `<dialog>`. |
| `click-non-interactive` | Put `@click` on `<button>` or `<a>`, or add `role` and `tabindex`. |
| `heading` | Do not skip heading levels. |
| `single-h1` | Use one `<h1>` per page (`<if>`/`<else>` branches count separately). |
| `tabindex` | Use only `0` or `-1`. |
| `duplicate-id` | Use a unique `id` per page. |
| `iframe-title` | Add `title` to `<iframe>`. |
| `a-no-href` | Add `href` to every `<a>`. Use `<button>` for actions. |

`:<attr>` and `{}` count as setting the attribute (`:aria-label="task.title"`, `aria-label="Remove {task.title}"`).

## WebMCP (`webmcp/*`, active when `"webmcp": true`)

Every `<form>` is an agent tool (`webmcp.md`).
- Errors: `webmcp/pair`, `webmcp/name`, `webmcp/duplicate`, `webmcp/param-name`, `webmcp/dynamic`, `webmcp/notool`, `webmcp/attribute`. With `"webmcp": false`, any tool attribute triggers `webmcp/disabled`.
- Warnings (errors with `--strict`): `webmcp/form-tool`, `webmcp/name-style`, `webmcp/description`, `webmcp/param-description`, `webmcp/autosubmit`.

## `dist/`

| Path | Use |
|---|---|
| `client/` | HTML per route and assets. |
| `server/worker.js` + `wrangler.jsonc` | Cloudflare Workers (resolves param pages via manifest, serves `_404.html` with 404, and serves `/assets/*` as `immutable`). Emitted when the app has a `*.server.js` or a `public/**/*.md`. `run_worker_first` sends every request, also prebuilt pages, through the worker, so middleware runs for them. `html_handling: "drop-trailing-slash"` serves `/a/index.html` at `/a` (200, no redirect to `/a/`). |
| `server/node.mjs` | Run `node dist/server/node.mjs` (reads `PORT`, default 3000). Emitted when the app has a `*.server.js`. |

Every server (`dev`, `serve`, Workers, Node) returns the matching `.md` from `public/` when `Accept` prefers `text/markdown` (`webmcp.md`).

## Deploy

Cloudflare Workers is the default target. Deploy only when the user asks. Use another target (Node, static hosting) only when the user asks for it.

### Before the first deploy

1. Set `name` in `pragma.json` to a unique Worker name (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). The name becomes the Worker name and the `<name>.<account>.workers.dev` URL. A deploy replaces any Worker with the same name in the account, so do not keep the starter name `app`. If the user gave no name, ask.
2. Run `pragma check --strict`, then `pragma build`. Fix all errors.
3. If `dist/server/wrangler.jsonc` does not exist (no `*.server.js` and no `public/**/*.md`), add `public/index.md` (`webmcp.md`) and build again. Without the worker, Workers cannot serve param pages (`[id].html`) or `_404.html`. Tell the user about the new file.
4. Log in to Cloudflare. Local: `npx wrangler@4 login`. CI: set `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`. Do not write tokens into files.

### Deploy

```sh
pragma build
npx wrangler@4 deploy --config dist/server/wrangler.jsonc
```

Wrangler prints the URL. Then check:
- `curl -I <url>` returns 200 and `curl -I <url>/missing-page` returns 404.
- `curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' <url>` returns markdown when `public/index.md` exists.
- `npx wrangler@4 tail <name>` shows the live logs (`logs.md`).

### Secrets, variables, bindings, domain

`pragma build` rewrites `dist/`. Do not edit `dist/server/wrangler.jsonc`. For more configuration, create `wrangler.jsonc` in the app root. Use the same `name` as `pragma.json` and point to `dist/`. Keep only the keys the app uses:

```jsonc
{
  "name": "my-app",
  "main": "dist/server/worker.js",
  "compatibility_date": "2025-11-01",
  "assets": { "directory": "dist/client", "binding": "ASSETS", "html_handling": "drop-trailing-slash", "run_worker_first": true },
  "vars": { "PRAGMA_LOG_LEVEL": "info" },
  "d1_databases": [{ "binding": "DB", "database_name": "my-app", "database_id": "<id>" }],
  "kv_namespaces": [{ "binding": "KV", "id": "<id>" }],
  "r2_buckets": [{ "binding": "FILES", "bucket_name": "my-app" }],
  "routes": [{ "pattern": "app.example.com", "custom_domain": true }]
}
```

Keep `"html_handling": "drop-trailing-slash"` in `assets`. Without it, Workers answers `/a` with a 307 to `/a/` (the build writes `a/index.html`).

Then deploy with `npx wrangler@4 deploy` (no `--config`).

| Need | Do | Read in `.server.js` |
|---|---|---|
| Secret (API key, token) | `npx wrangler@4 secret put KEY_NAME --name <name>`. Never put a secret in `vars` or in a file. | `env.KEY_NAME` |
| Plain variable | `vars` in the root `wrangler.jsonc`. | `env.NAME` |
| SQL database (D1) | `npx wrangler@4 d1 create <db>`, then binding `DB`. | `db.get`, `db.all`, `db.run` |
| Key-value store (KV) | `npx wrangler@4 kv namespace create <ns>`, then binding `KV`. | `kv.get`, `kv.put`, `kv.delete` |
| File storage (R2) | `npx wrangler@4 r2 bucket create <bucket>`, then binding `FILES`. | `files.get`, `files.put`, `files.delete` |
| Custom domain | `routes` with `custom_domain: true`. The zone must be in the same Cloudflare account. | |
| Log export (OTLP) | `OTEL_*` in `vars`, headers with a token as a secret (`logs.md`). | |

`load` and actions receive `env`, `db`, `kv`, and `files`. In `pragma dev` and `pragma serve`, `env` is the process environment (`KEY_NAME=value pragma dev`), and `db`, `kv`, and `files` are `undefined`. Check them before use.

### Bindings in dev (`pragma dev --cf`)

`pragma dev --cf` gives `.server.js` the bindings of the root `wrangler.jsonc` through wrangler `getPlatformProxy`: `vars`, secrets from `.dev.vars`, D1, KV, R2, `send_email`, rate limits, `ctx.waitUntil` and `caches`. Bindings with `"remote": true` use the real Cloudflare resource (log in first: `npx wrangler@4 login`); the others run locally with state in `.wrangler/` (exclude it from git).

1. Install wrangler in the app: `npm i -D wrangler@4`.
2. Create the root `wrangler.jsonc` (above).
3. Run `pragma dev --cf`.

Without `--cf`, `pragma dev` is unchanged. A change to `wrangler.jsonc` or `.dev.vars` restarts the node server. On Node, only `env` from `cloudflare:workers` works; other `cloudflare:*` exports throw when used (`packages.md`).

### Workers runtime limits

- There is no filesystem. Do not use `node:fs`, `process.cwd()`, or paths on disk in `.server.js`. Import JSON with `import products from './_products.json' with { type: 'json' }`.
- Read configuration from `env`, not `process.env`.
- The generated config has no `nodejs_compat`. If a package needs `node:*` modules, add `"compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"]` to the root `wrangler.jsonc` and tell the user.
- If a feature cannot work on Workers, stop and tell the user before you change the target.
- WebSocket endpoints (`status: 101`) work only on Workers. `pragma dev` and `pragma serve` run Node and cannot upgrade; test them with `npx wrangler@4 dev --config dist/server/wrangler.jsonc`.

### CI (GitHub Actions)

Install the CLI version from `.pragma/version`, so `pragma build` does not stop with `app/core-outdated`:

```yaml
name: Deploy
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
concurrency:
  group: deploy
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Install pragma
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leonavas/pragma/main/install.sh | PRAGMA_VERSION="$(cat .pragma/version)" sh
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
        if: hashFiles('package-lock.json') != ''
      - run: pragma check --strict
      - run: pragma build
      - run: npx --yes wrangler@4 deploy --config dist/server/wrangler.jsonc
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
```

With a root `wrangler.jsonc`, remove `--config dist/server/wrangler.jsonc`. The API token needs the "Edit Cloudflare Workers" template permissions.
